name: boundary-fidelity
tool: same reflection harness run against both revisions (identical denominator: every item.Item field minus the seven the boundary re-supplies); getbytes is the get render of an archived ADR with context/decision/consequences/status populated
note: v3 adds the CALLER-ROUTE check v2 was missing. v2 measured through lastReject and Tombstone - the API - and an independent validator pointed out that for an ARCHIVED record no caller route showed any of it: get rendered only the record line, so the API number overstated what anyone could actually see. The reject path was already honest there, because revocation writes the item back into work.md. Fixed by giving gets live and archived branches one shared substance renderer. That exposed the ADR fields rendering twice - once from the body text the old adrOutcome folded them into, once as fields - and retiring that fold removed the shared body/field budget whose contention had produced the same amputation defect three times. getbytes is unchanged at 260 for an ADR (same content, different source) and a non-ADR kind gains the structural lines it previously could not show at all, so the fix is token-neutral where it overlaps and additive only where it recovers something. Second methodology lesson in one task: measure through the route the caller uses, not the one the code exposes.

name: curation-fidelity
tool: three-conflict curation fixture (two source repos answer three questions differently; export, apply both, answer each, archive each, compact apply=true; then probe recoverability)
note: Measures the only thing this feature exists to guarantee: after a curated conflict has been decided and the record archived, can both the chosen and the rejected decision still be read? Round 1 scored ZERO on every axis - archive() retained a tombstone body only for kind=research, and a decide-minted ADRs first body line is the machine field kind: radio, so all three decisions compressed to the byte-identical contentless summary and both sides of each vanished from get, work.md and find. Round 2 recovers all six values (three losers via find scope=history, three winners via the tombstones decision: field) and the same run drops duplicate mints from 3 to 0, because entry identity is now recomputed from content instead of trusted off the wire. The fixture is the full lifecycle including compact apply=true, since the projects own housekeeping was one of the routes to the loss.

name: judged-friction
tool: two instruments. calls/done/worst: four independent agents per run given only the 15-line tricky brief and the metered CLI, no docs, no source. bytes: spectackle bench -baseline OLD -against NEW, the deterministic scripted A/B, with BOTH sides built -buildvcs=false
note: v3 CORRECTS v2s byte measurement, which was an artifact and claimed the opposite sign. v2 built the candidate inside a git worktree and the baseline in a plain clone; that changes what ResolvedVersion stamps and swings the #version line by ~34B per render, which is how a +B change was reported as -48B. Built with -buildvcs=false on both sides the honest figure is +142B, ~+36 tokens, candidate LOSES - after compressing rules three JSON templates to one requiredness line and drafts shape to a field list, which took it down from +210B. Second measurement error of this session, both of the same kind: an instrument compared against itself under different conditions. The judged calls figure for the shapes run is 0 because it was never obtained - twelve agents across three attempts died on API 529 - and must be read as ABSENT, not as an improvement. So the discoverability change is byte-negative on the only metric available and unproven on the metric that would justify it. It is retained rather than reverted only because the mechanism is separately evidenced: 8 of the 79 before-run calls were shape rediscovery, and one recovered call in this scenario is worth 200-400B against the 142B cost. That is expected value, not measurement, and the task stays open until a judged run settles it.

name: lifecycle-tokens

name: online-edge-render
note: Green-path g-line surface of one full online lifecycle (activation+done+archive), measured from the real v0.5.5 renders of PR 195/197 vs the RENDER-PARITY-001 diet single-artifact lines (same URL/SHA lengths). -377B, about -94 tokens per online lifecycle - the online counterpart of the offline collapse M-01KYJWFQ8SE68. name: outcome-navigation
note: n=3 fresh sonnet judges, outcome scenario, v0.6.2 (in-loop VAC finding + delegation-aware detector under test). VALIDITY 1/3 to 3/3: the vacuous-test trap fired ZERO times after voiding 2 of 3 in BOTH prior batches - judges wrote asserting, table-driven, race-tested suites (j1 39 calls/~1016 tok 5/5, j2 38/~1159 4/5, j3 43/~1635 4/5, all rounds=0 asks=0). name: tricky-navigation
note: n=3 fresh sonnet judges, tricky scenario (rule slots, reopen loop into blocked, decide exit), v0.6.0. FIRST fully valid batch: j1 18 calls/~570 tok, j2 30/~1056, j3 27/~925 - all authored a lint-clean rule, drove the rounds exhaustion into blocked, resolved the auto-minted ADR via decide (rescope) and ended check ok, from renders alone with zero user asks. name: worktree-navigation
note: n=3 fresh sonnet judges, worktree scenario (the dedicated swarm flow: start-lease, in-worktree edit, submit gate-integrate-merge-replay), v0.6.3. VALIDITY 3/3 - second consecutive fully valid batch (j1 40 calls/~1625 tok, j2 22/~617, j3 44/~1516; all change=true task=done flow=true check=true). Hypotheses held: submit navigated from renders alone; each judge hit the WT identity refusal exactly once and recovered in one step from its hint (v0.5.3 fixes hold in the identity-centric scenario); the v0.6.0 diet renders cost nothing. j3 exceeded the brief: noticed the fixture rule API-STATUS-001 semantically contradicted the requested change and edited the rule to match.
